gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant strengthening of prior year reserves totaling GBP 44.240 million, representing 100.52% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This adverse development was primarily driven by the 2016 and 2015 underwriting years. For the 2016 year of account, there was a substantial strengthening of GBP 43.683 million, largely due to the impact of Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria (HIMM), as well as other large losses and attritional claims in excess of plan, particularly affecting cargo, hull, and property accounts. The 2015 year of account also saw a strengthening of GBP 0.557 million, attributed to large losses, catastrophe losses, and higher than expected attritional claims in the hull and property accounts.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 Jan 2017 were GBP 44.009m. The report does not disclose a single aggregate quantified prior-year reserve movement for 2017; reserve movements are discussed by class and driven materially by natural catastrophes (notably Hurricanes Harvey/Irma/Maria and the Mexican earthquake), several large individual losses (including a GBP 1.6m hull loss in 2015 and cargo/property catastrophes) and changes in attritional experience. The syndicate also completed an RITC (2015 into 2016) on 1 Jan 2018 transferring technical provisions of GBP 7.4m. Overall the narrative describes a mixture of adverse developments from catastrophe and large losses and improvements in attritional loss ratios in some classes, so the net picture is mixed across lines.
raw_causal_phrases: GBP 3.1m impact from HIMM in relation to policies which incepted in 2016 and were in force at the time of these events.
The net impact of HIMM is GBP 12.5m.
These losses were caused by a combination of a large loss of GBP 1.6m and a higher than expected incidence of attritional claims.

The property account ran at a net loss ratio of 117% and sustained a net underwriting loss of GBP 0.5m. Contributing to this loss were two catastrophe losses which impacted the portfolio disproportionately.
In the 2015 year of account, the attritional loss ratio was 82%, improving slightly to 81% in 2016 and currently performing at 57% in 2017.

On 1st January 2018, the 2015 year of account was closed by a Reinsurance to close agreement (RITC) into the 2016 year of account. The value of the technical provisions transferred, which formed part of this agreement was GBP 7.4 million.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: No single explicit aggregate prior-year reserve movement figure is provided in the report (no 'movement in prior year's provision' aggregate is stated). The claims development triangle is present but RITC activity (2015 closed into 2016 with a GBP 7.4m transfer disclosed) and the mix of direct and reinsurance business complicate using the triangle for a reliable PVY aggregate. LOB movement amounts were derived by comparing gross claims outstanding by LOB between 2016 and 2017 (computed from the concentration table) and therefore represent changes in outstanding balances, not necessarily 'prior-year development' in the strict sense. Confidence levels and nulls are indicated where data was not explicitly stated.
